issues.description: Default branch in sign_message silently maps unknown modes to CHIP_0002 instead of refusing
issues.detail: In chia/wallet/util/signing.py, sign_message uses an if/elif chain that falls through to CHIP_0002 for any unrecognized SigningMode. verify_signature correctly raises ValueError on unknown modes. This asymmetry is bad taste: identical inputs should be handled symmetrically. Make both raise, or both default, but pick one.

issues.description: signing_mode_enum free function duplicates logic that belongs on the request dataclasses
issues.detail: VerifySignature got a signing_mode_enum @property, but SignMessageByAddress/SignMessageByID get a separate module-level function doing the same job. Pick one shape. A free function plus a property for sibling types is the kind of inconsistency the maintainer-six-years-from-now curses. Make it a property on both, or a function for both.

issues.description: signing.py imports VerifySignatureResponse from wallet_request_types creating a layering tangle
issues.detail: A util module returns a response type defined in the RPC request-types module. That is backwards: utilities should not depend on RPC wire types. Either move VerifySignatureResponse down to the util, or have verify_signature return a plain (bool, str|None) and let the RPC layer wrap it. Otherwise every consumer of the util drags in RPC types.

issues.description: SignMessageResponse is a new dataclass duplicating an existing tuple shape with no added value
issues.detail: The old methods returned tuple[G1Element, G2Element]. The new util introduces a frozen dataclass with the same two fields. Gratuitous abstraction unless a caller actually benefits. If the only consumer is the RPC layer destructuring two fields, a tuple is fine; if the dataclass exists for clarity, fine, but justify it.

issues.description: verify_signature docstring references a nonexistent :param request:
issues.detail: The function takes keyword args (signing_mode, public_key, message, signature, address) but the docstring says ':param request:'. Either the docstring was copy-pasted from an older signature or the function was refactored without updating it. Small, but exactly the kind of staleness that misleads the next reader.

issues.description: Variable named hex_message holds non-hex bytes in two of four branches
issues.detail: In sign_message and the old code, hex_message is bound to UTF-8 bytes and to a tree-hash digest, neither of which is meaningfully 'hex'. The name was misleading in the original and was copied into the new util. Rename to message_bytes or to_sign. Carrying forward a bad name during an extract-to-library is a missed opportunity.

review.summary: The extract-to-library is the right shape and the new tests for sign_message_by_id are overdue and welcome. The util itself, however, ships with avoidable rough edges: asymmetric default-mode handling between sign and verify, a layering inversion where the util imports an RPC response type, and inconsistent placement of signing_mode_enum (property on one type, free function on the siblings). A new dataclass replaces a tuple with no clear gain, a misleading hex_message name is preserved verbatim, and the verify_signature docstring references a parameter that does not exist. NEEDS-WORK: fix the symmetry and the layering before landing; the rest are nits worth cleaning up while the file is open.
